conflicts: Brief Alignment proposes: Preserve the exact 8×8 starting position and all 32 pieces, but give white and black pieces unmistakably different fills/outlines while retaining classic glyph silhouettes. Additional literal detail can increase one-off components and rough exceptions unless each addition is expressed through the established construction system. Clarity proposes: Consolidate the side panel into a continuous hierarchy: title/context, current turn, a clearly bounded move-history table with readable headers and rows, then controls immediately beneath it. Changing scale and contrast for hierarchy is useful, but ad hoc emphasis must not introduce unrelated borders, shadows, typography, or spacing. Expressiveness proposes: Develop a distinctive modern-club identity through bespoke piece silhouettes, subtle rank/file ornament, and meaningful turn or last-move emphasis; give the side panel tournament-card details and material indicators that add character without compromising classical legibility. Extra shapes, textures, glows, and differentiated treatments can fragment palette, geometry, and material logic if each becomes a bespoke exception.
accept: Accept every fidelity restoration, hierarchy correction, and thematic differentiation that can be built from shared grid, type, palette, stroke, radius, elevation, and illustration tokens. Accept stronger focal contrast and a distinctive hero treatment, but keep their construction precise and reuse their rules in related states.
compromise: Implement the craft foundation first: Normalize every piece glyph to a consistent optical bounding box, baseline, stroke/shadow treatment, and contrast strategy; make white and black sets equally crisp rather than stylistically asymmetric. Map every required or expressive addition onto a small documented token set, while allowing deliberate scale and color-role differences for hierarchy. Use one exceptional hero treatment at most; all supporting components must share alignment, typography, outline, lighting, and spacing rules, with clipping and viewport-edge defects resolved.
